title: Chiral Cavity Vacua as Local Generators and Probes of Non-Abelian Kitaev Topology
abstract: We show how a gyrotropic cavity vacuum generates, probes, and spatially programs non-Abelian topology in the Kitaev honeycomb model. Gauge-consistent virtual-photon elimination produces a universal helicity-odd interaction $\mathrm{i}[P_x,P_y]$ alongside same-order even dressing. For the leading bond polarization, this commutator is exactly the Kitaev three-spin mass. Mode normalization imposes a thermodynamic constraint: one extended normalized mode gives a local mass that vanishes with sample area, whereas a localized mode writes a finite topological island and a finite mode density enables a bulk mass. The exact Majorana solution yields helicity-reversed Chern gaps and edge propagation, while integrated circular dichroism exactly measures the mass generator, $\langle\mathrm{i}[P_x,P_y]\rangle=-\sqrt3p^2\langle O_3\rangle$. Real-space calculations reveal a non-Abelian island and a helicity wall with two co-propagating Majorana modes. Uniform helicity reversal is a Dirac-mass quench with $n_{\rm ex}\proptoτ_Q^{-1}$, whereas moving a wall localizes the gap closing. The equilibrium vacuum kernel contains sum-frequency rather than resonant denominators. These results establish distinct criteria for local and bulk cavity-induced topology.
summary: This theoretical work shows how coupling a Kitaev model to a chiral cavity vacuum generates a non-Abelian topological mass term. By analyzing spectral properties via circular dichroism, the authors distinguish between local topological islands and the conditions necessary to achieve a true, bulk, cavity-induced topological state.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether a stationary chiral vacuum can generate the specific mass required for the non-Abelian Kitaev phase, and whether this induced mass is an intensive bulk property or merely a finite-size/local effect.
main_result: The chiral vacuum generates the Kitaev three-spin mass via a helicity-odd commutator, demonstrating that localized modes create finite non-Abelian islands, while bulk mass requires a finite local density of chiral modes.
method: The analysis uses virtual-photon elimination and calculates a diagnostic sum rule derived from circular dichroism ($\Delta A$), which exactly measures the generated chiral interaction $\langle i[P_x, P_y] angle$.
model_or_system: The system is based on the Kitaev honeycomb model coupled to a cavity photon field, analyzed using effective Hamiltonians derived via second-order projection and incorporating the dipole self-energy (DSE).
key_observables: The helicity-odd commutator $\langle i[P_x, P_y] angle$, the gap $\Delta_M$, the Chern number $C_{	ext{occ}}$, and the local/bulk mass generation.
important_parameters: The cavity coupling strength ($\kappa_{cav}$), the hopping parameters ($J_x, J_y, J_z$), and the ratio of energy scales defining the controlled hierarchy.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a controlled hierarchy of energy scales (e.g., $\lVert T Vert, \hbar\omega_c, \lVert H_s Vert \ll \Delta_{	ext{ch}}$) and treats the vacuum term and probe absorption using different denominators.
figures_summary: Figures compare the scaling of local mass for localized vs. extended modes, show the gap opening and reversal of Majorana Chern numbers based on cavity helicity, and illustrate the spatial programming of Ising topology.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by deriving the effective Hamiltonian from the full microscopic model, establishing the diagnostic sum rule via circular dichroism, and then analyzing the implications for local versus bulk topological mass generation.
why_interesting: This work bridges concepts from topological phases (Kitaev model) with cavity QED/open quantum systems, providing a concrete mechanism (vacuum polarization) to engineer topological order, which is highly relevant for AMO physics.
